question: When an edit deletes every character under a published comment, should the thread survive, and how should document and comment history interact?
method: best-api-review/history-v2; direct Google Docs UI inspection; official Google and Notion documentation; current source and focused proof
trigger: User requested a Google Docs and Notion comparison, a harsh API verdict, and a full analysis of history behavior.
requirements: Deleting all anchored document characters must not silently destroy a published conversation.
Document undo, redo, and revision restore must map or recover anchors without rewinding comment data.
Draft cancellation, empty message edits, resolve, reopen, message deletion, and thread deletion need distinct semantics.
A thread with deleted source content must remain discoverable and actionable from comment history.
Suggestion decisions and ordinary comments need one history projection without merging their storage owners.
The editor package owns current thread records and anchor mapping; applications own persistence, authorization, retention, and cross-document history queries.
History must scale without loading every document revision or all comment activity into the live editor.
evidenceReuse: Reused the accepted package-data ownership decision and its source map. Replayed the current deleted-range unit/component proof and the focused Chromium history case. Inspected the supplied Google Doc comment-history and version-history surfaces instead of creating new test content.
summary: Preserve every published thread when its annotated text is deleted. Keep its last excerpt and a collapsed or detached mapped target, show it in comment history as deleted source content, and let undo or a historical document projection restore the anchor. Keep document revisions, comment activity, and retained suggestion decisions as separate durable authorities joined by a history read model. Current Plate already preserves collapsed anchors through repeated undo/redo; it lacks the durable activity/tombstone data required for a truthful history product.
alternatives: Delete the thread with its anchor: reject; a reversible document edit would cause irreversible conversation loss and remote editors could erase other people’s discussion.
Auto-resolve the thread: reject; removing text does not prove the question was answered, and Google Docs keeps original-content-deleted items visible in comment history.
Keep only the current collapsed range: keep as the live-editor projection, but insufficient for durable history because resolve, reopen, edit, deletion, actor, and time are overwritten or discarded.
Put comments inside editor undo/version history: reject; document restoration must not roll conversation state backward or resurrect deleted message content.

Add a second history plugin or duplicate thread store: reject; comments owns conversation state, authored owns edit decisions, and an application history read model should join their immutable activity.
Preserve a compact thread aggregate plus append-only activity/tombstones and per-document-revision target projections: pursue.
proofLimits: The supplied Google Doc was inspected read-only. It directly showed open and resolved suggestions, original-content-deleted entries, explicit resolve/delete actions, and a separate version-history surface; no new external comment was posted and no live regular-comment anchor was deleted. Google official help documents lifecycle and export, while the exact anchor-deletion evidence also includes a Google support community report. Notion official documentation proves explicit comment lifecycle, a comments pane, and a page timeline containing revisions and comments, but does not document the exact inline-anchor deletion result; no Notion workspace was mutated. Current Plate proof passed 29 focused unit/component tests and the single Chromium case for fully deleted comment history. This is a review record, not an implementation.
